title: By the river Chebar (Ezekiel 1)
hookLine: among exiles in Babylon, a vision of a chariot of fire and wheels
last: THERE WERE ADDED BESIDES UNTO THEM MANY LIKE WORDS.

cards: Where does God live? For many in Judah, the answer had an address: Jerusalem, the Temple, the holy of holies. Now some of them have been carried off to Babylon.
They sit by the river Chebar, a long way from that address. Among them is Ezekiel, whom the text calls a priest, far from the Temple where priests serve.
And his book opens there, in the King James words: "as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God." Not in Jerusalem. In exile.

teach.b: What Ezekiel sees is hard to describe, and he knows it. A whirlwind comes out of the north, a great cloud, fire folding in on itself, a glow like bright metal at the center.
Out of it come four living creatures, each with four faces: a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle. They have wings, and they move straight ahead without turning.

teach.h: A WHEEL IN THE MIDDLE OF A WHEEL.
teach.b: Beside them are wheels, as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel, their rims full of eyes. Wherever the spirit goes, the wheels go too.

Above is a firmament like crystal, then a throne, and on it a figure like a man, surrounded by brightness like a rainbow in the clouds. Listen to how careful the language is. Ezekiel almost never says this is what it was.
He says the appearance of, the likeness of, as it were.

teach.h: THE APPEARANCE OF THE LIKENESS OF THE GLORY.
teach.b: At the top, he piles them up: "This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD." Three layers of distance before the name of God. Jewish tradition calls this vision the merkavah, the chariot.

The Mishnah treats it with great caution: it is not to be taught even to one student, unless he is wise and already understands on his own. Mystics later built a whole path of contemplation around it.
But the plain meaning is enough for today.
The throne has wheels. The glory that seemed tied to one building shows up beside a river in a foreign land, right there with the exiles.

how: Jews read Ezekiel 1 as the opening of the book of Ezekiel, and in many communities it is chanted as the prophetic reading on the first day of Shavuot.

games.q: you're Ezekiel, a priest far from the Temple. the sky opens over a river in Babylon. how do you describe what you see?
o: say exactly what God looks like.
describe it as the appearance of a likeness.
games.why: he describes it in careful layers: the appearance, the likeness, as it were. he writes it down without claiming to capture it.

practice: If you can, go to a window or step outside, and find something in motion: a cloud, a bird, branches, even a ceiling fan.

Just watch it move, without naming or explaining it; Ezekiel was standing in an ordinary place, by a river in a foreign land, when the sky opened. If you pray, you can pray from right where you are, the way the exiles had to.

wordCard.voice: Merkavah. The chariot: the name Jewish tradition gives to Ezekiel's vision of the throne with wheels, seen among exiles by the river Chebar. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: chariot, the name tradition gives to Ezekiel's throne vision.

carryVoice: Your line: God in exile too. The throne has wheels, and it came to the river. See you tomorrow.
